# Fixed React movement unit data

This is synthetic protocol input, not publication approval, learner observation,
or evidence that the current candidate's React course compiled.

The generator compiled the protected `21dcc855413a56729206b02c5a03701207123699`
snapshot once and exported only four existing goals: initial Props, quiz Props,
quiz State, and the independent quiz capstone. Their 30 authored fixtures include
the exact 25 moved obligations (8 + 9 + 8). Initial Props has 5 fixtures and the
approved two explanatory step changes. No Reading, temperature, Form compose,
or Effect compose lesson is included.

The JSON contains four runtime lessons, four complete authoring exercises, eight
referenced glossary entries, public provenance, and four SVG byte payloads.
The exact generator source is retained in `.generator.txt`; its hash, source
file manifest, fixed IDs/profiles/counts, learner digests and data digest are
checked by `reactMovementFixture.ts`. That loader does not fetch Git objects or
compile `content/react`. The historical source commit is provenance only, so CI
does not require unpublished Git history.

For the movement protocol, the loader assembles a neutral six-slot envelope:
three destinations, the initial lesson, and two reused-ID source slots made
from the same old Props/State data with the existing typed inverse mapper.
Those slots retain the tests that require fresh approval at reused IDs, even
when content looks identical. They are not new curriculum goals or a public
course. Every original test assertion and the 53+10 / 28+10 / 25 obligations
remain in place.

Actual prepare, archived-source readers, qualification, and `content/react`
are unchanged. They continue consuming the complete real course inventory.

To regenerate, Root uses the stored generator in an isolated broad21 staging
tree with the source manifest embedded in this JSON; the generator belongs at
`tests/local/` while running. Regeneration is a deliberate local operation,
not a CI dependency or a learner acceptance procedure.
